title: Disome-seq Protocol for Identifying Ribosome Collisions in Yeast Cells
author: Ayres-Galhardo, Marks, et al.
materials:
CRITICAL: Phenol and chloroform are particularly hazardous substances, wear gloves, lab coat, and safety glasses during these experiments.
CRITICAL: The steps 36–45 need to be performed in a chemical fume hood.
36.Set up tubes for acid phenol/chloroform extraction.a.Prepare and label two 1.5 mL screw cap tubes per each sample (that has 1 mL sucrose gradient fraction) and fill them with 375 μL of acid phenol.b.Heat the tubes with acid phenol at 65°C for 10 minutes in a thermomixer.c.Prepare and label one 2 mL screw cap tube per each sample, fill it with 700 μL of acid phenol, and leave at room temperature.d.Prepare and label one 1.5 mL screw cap tube per each sample, fill it with 600 μL of chloroform, and leave at room temperature.37.Add 57.1 μL of 20% SDS per 1 mL of the collected sucrose fraction and heat the tubes at 65°C to dissolve SDS while inverting the tube several times to ensure mixing.38.Once the fraction + SDS becomes clear, add 500 μL of it to each of the two pre-heated phenol tubes prepared in Step 36a-b.a.Incubate for 2 min at 65°C, and vortex.b.Incubate for 2 min at 65°C, and vortex.c.Incubate for 1 min at 65°C.39.Place the samples on ice and incubate for 5 minutes.40.Spin for 2 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at room temperature.41.Pull the aqueous layer.a.Pipette out the bottom layer in each tube into the 2 mL screw cap tube that contains 700 μL of room temperature acid phenol (prepared in Step 36c) by combining two tubes per each sample into one tube.Note: Because of high concentration of sucrose, the aqueous layer is at the bottom instead of top.b.Vortex for 5 minutes by using a disruptor that can hold multiple tubes.42.Spin for 2 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at room temperature.43.Pull the aqueous layer.a.Pipette out the bottom layer in each tube into the 1.5 mL screw cap tube that contains 600 μL of room temperature chloroform (prepared in Step 36d).Note: Because of high concentration of sucrose, the aqueous layer is at the bottom instead of top.b.Vortex for 30 seconds.Note: If the sample looks cloudy, place them back in the 65°C thermomixer for 1 minute before removing the aqueous layer.44.Spin for 2 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at room temperature.45.Pull the top aqueous layer (∼1 mL) into 15 mL tubes on ice.46.Prepare the precipitation reaction and place the tubes in −80°C for 30 minutes.a.During this incubation, pre-cool a microcentrifuge to 4°C and prepare 3 x 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes per each sample.

Note: You can also leave the samples at −80°C for overnight precipitation.

47.Thaw the precipitation reaction tubes at room temperature and separate each into 3 x 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.48.Spin for 30 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at 4°C.49.Remove the supernatant and wash the white pellet containing RNA with 750 μL 80% cold ethanol.50.Spin for 5 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at 4°C.51.Remove the supernatant with a P1000 pipettor, quick spin the samples on a benchtop mini centrifuge, then remove the rest of the supernatant with a P200 pipettor.52.Air dry the pellets for 10 minutes at room temperature by leaving the microcentrifuge tube lids open, and visually check to ensure that the pellet is fully dry.53.Resuspend the pellets with 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 and combine the three tubes into one.a.For disome samples, resuspend one of the three tubes with 7 μL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 and then use this resuspension to resuspend the pellets from two other tubes (total volume is 7 μL).b.For monosome samples, resuspend each of the three tubes with 7 μL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 and then combine them all into a single tube (total volume is 21 μL).54.Dilute the samples 1:20 (0.5 μL of the sample + 9.5 μL water) and measure A260 and A260/A280 values.
Pause Point: These RNA samples can be kept at −80°C indefinitely.

55.Determine the volume that corresponds to a maximum of 5 μg of RNA from Step 54 and aliquot it into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Note: If the sample volume is smaller than 10 μL, dilute the sample with 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 to 10 μL.
Note: Libraries can be successfully prepared with samples that have as low as 500 ng input material.

59.Incubate samples, markers and RNA ladder for 2 minutes at 80°C, and then place immediately on ice.60.Prepare and load the size selection gel.a.Place a 15% TBE-Urea gel in a tank filled with 1X TBE.CRITICAL: Polyacrylamide gels can contain acrylamide, which is neurotoxic.b.Clean the wells of the gel by pipetting up and down to each well with a P1000 pipette.c.Load the entire sample, 7 μL of size markers at each end of the gel, 2.5 μL of RNA ladder at each end of the gel and 5 μL of the color dye at one of the empty wells.d.Leave empty wells between samples to avoid cross-contamination.e.Load all empty wells with 5 μL 2X TBU.Note: See Figure 8 for an example size selection gel.Figure 8Example of size selection gelsSize selection gels of Ribo-seq (A) and Disome-seq (B) samples.RNA ladder sizes are shown with black lines. Size markers for Ribo-seq (25-34mers) and Disome-seq (54-68mers) are indicated on each gel image. The gel pieces encompassing the area of the size marker at other lanes are cut for extraction (lower panel).61.Run the gel at 7 or 15 Watts constant for 1 or 2 gels, respectively, until front dye (bromophenol blue) reaches the bottom of the gel, while the trailing dye (xylene cyanol) is still at the top.62.Remove the gel out of its cassette and stain it with 1X SYBR Gold solution by shaking it for 5 minutes while covered in foil.63.Transfer the gel onto a transparent plastic laser printer sheet and cover it with a Saran Wrap.64.Image the gel using an imager system that has a SYBR Gold setting and a blue light transilluminator for placing the gel, and save the uncut gel image.
Note: Blue light transilluminator must be used to avoid potential ultraviolet light damage of the RNA.
65.Place the gel on a blue light transilluminator and cut the region of the sample in line with the outer edges of the corresponding size markers by using a razor blade.
Note: See Figure 8 for an example cut gel.
66.Place the cut gel piece into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.67.Once the sample lanes are cut, then cut the size markers as well and place them into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube (25+34 and 54+68 nucleotide size markers combined as monosome and disome footprint marker, respectively).68.Add 500 μL RNA Gel Extraction Buffer to each tube and freeze them in −80°C for 30 minutes.
Pause Point: The buffer-frozen gel pieces can be kept at −80°C indefinitely.
69.Place the tubes with buffer-frozen gel pieces in a thermomixer that is set to 22°C, 700 rpm overnight.70.Next day, briefly spin down samples by using a benchtop mini centrifuge and transfer the supernatant to a fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Note: Avoid getting any gel pieces into the fresh tube and repeat the spin if you observe any small gel pieces.
71.Start precipitation of RNA.a.Add 2 μL glycoblue and 500 μL isopropanol to each tube.b.Mix well by inverting the tube 8 times.c.Place samples on ice and incubate for 1 hour.72.Spin for 30 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at 4°C.73.Remove the supernatant and wash the blue pellet with 750 μL 80% cold ethanol.74.Spin for 3 minutes at full speed (21,000 x g) at 4°C.75.Remove the supernatant with a P1000 pipettor, quick spin the samples on a benchtop mini centrifuge, then remove the rest of the supernatant with a P200 pipettor.76.Air dry the pellets for 10 minutes at room temperature by leaving the microcentrifuge tube lids open, and visually check to ensure that the pellet is fully dry.77.Resuspend the pellets with 3.5 μL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0.
Pause Point: These RNA samples can be kept at −80°C indefinitely.

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Mix Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 (20 mM, 200 µL of 1 M stock), KCl (140 mM, 700 µL of 2 M stock), MgCl₂ (1.5 mM, 15 µL of 1 M stock), Triton X‑100 (1 % v/v, 1 mL of 10 % stock), cycloheximide (0.1 mg/mL, 100 µL of 10 mg/mL stock) and RNase‑free water to a final volume of 10 mL. Keep on ice; cycloheximide is toxic, Triton X‑100 is an irritant.

steps.title: Make frozen lysis buffer droplets
steps.instruction: For each sample, prepare a 50 mL conical tube with four 21‑gauge holes at the bottom, place tubes in liquid nitrogen (5–10 mL level), add 750 µL lysis buffer dropwise (raising pipette tip to avoid freezing inside tip and avoiding repeated drops in the same spot) to form frozen droplets, drain liquid nitrogen, cap tubes and store at –80 °C (indefinitely).

steps.title: Set up CryoMill program
steps.instruction: Connect CryoMill to a full liquid‑nitrogen tank, turn on, set program: auto pre‑cooling, then 9 cycles of 1 min grinding at 30 Hz followed by 2 min rest at 5 Hz; tighten sealing plug and lock nuts; run a test cycle (1–2 cycles) to confirm no error.

steps.title: Prepare 10X sucrose gradient buffer
steps.instruction: Combine Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 (200 mM, 4 mL of 1 M stock), KCl (1.5 M, 15 mL of 2 M stock), MgCl₂ (50 mM, 1 mL of 1 M stock), DTT (5 mM, 100 µL of 1 M fresh solution) and RNase‑free water to a final volume of 20.1 mL. DTT is an irritant; keep buffer on ice.

steps.title: Prepare 60 % sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 150 g sucrose in 100 mL RNase‑free water in a 250‑mL beaker on a hot plate with stirring, transfer to a measuring cylinder or volumetric flask and bring to 250 mL with RNase‑free water; filter‑sterilize through 0.22 µm filter and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % sucrose in gradient buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 6.6 mL 60 % sucrose, 4 mL 10X gradient buffer and 29.4 mL RNase‑free water to a final volume of 40 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 50 % sucrose in gradient buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 33.3 mL 60 % sucrose, 4 mL 10X gradient buffer and 2.7 mL RNase‑free water to a final volume of 40 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 80 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Combine 80 mL molecular‑biology‑grade 100 % ethanol with 20 mL RNase‑free water to make 100 mL of 80 % ethanol. Keep at –20 °C; ethanol is volatile and flammable.

steps.title: Prepare 10 mM Tris pH 8.0
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 with 9.9 mL RNase‑free water to 10 mL. Keep at room temperature for resuspending pellets after nucleic‑acid extractions.

steps.title: Prepare RNA gel extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 75 µL 3 M NaOAc, 1.5 µL 1 mM EDTA, 18.75 µL 0.25 % SDS and RNase‑free water to a final volume of 750 µL. SDS is an irritant; EDTA poses health hazards. Keep at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % bromophenol blue solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg bromophenol‑blue sodium salt in 10 mL RNase‑free water; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % xylene cyanol FF solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg xylene cyanol FF in 10 mL RNase‑free water; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % bromophenol blue solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg bromophenol‑blue sodium salt in 10 mL RNase‑free water; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % xylene cyanol FF solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg xylene cyanol FF in 10 mL RNase‑free water; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 2X TBU solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4.2 g urea and 1.2 g Ficoll 400 in 1 mL 10X TBE buffer, stir on a heated magnetic stirrer, then add RNase‑free water to a final volume of 10 mL. Aliquot 1 mL and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare SYBR Gold staining buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL 10,000X SYBR Gold stock, 10 µL 10X TBE and RNase‑free water to 100 mL (final 1X). Make 10 µL aliquots to minimize freeze‑thaw and light exposure.

steps.title: Prepare DNA gel extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 45 µL 5 M NaCl, 1.5 µL 1 mM EDTA, 7.5 µL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 and RNase‑free water to 750 µL. EDTA poses health hazards; keep at 4 °C for up to two weeks.

steps.title: Prepare 10X DNA gel loading buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 5 mL 100 % glycerol, 0.5 mL 1 % bromophenol‑blue, 0.5 mL 1 % xylene cyanol FF and RNase‑free water to 10 mL. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare yeast lysates in CryoMill
steps.instruction: a) On dry ice, number four 5 mL capsules and lids, place a capsule and lid on dry ice, add one 7 mm metal ball to capsule and one to lid. b) After 10 min cooling, transfer frozen cell scrapes (from growth/filtration) into each capsule using tweezers dipped briefly in liquid nitrogen; pour 750 µL frozen lysis‑buffer droplets into capsule; add the second metal ball, screw lid tightly (wear thin cryoprotection gloves). c) Dip the whole canister (containing up to four capsules) in liquid nitrogen for 1 min, keep on dry ice, then load into CryoMill grinding jar (ensure lids touch sealing lid, balance capsules if fewer than four). d) Unscrew sealing plug, loosen lock nut, insert grinding jar into cooling jacket, screw securely with opening aid and locking pin. e) Start liquid‑nitrogen flow, run the programmed auto pre‑cooling followed by 9 cycles of 1 min at 30 Hz and 2 min at 5 Hz rest; after 9 cycles manually restart to complete 18 cycles total. f) After milling, turn off LN₂ flow, remove grinding jar, unscrew lock nut, open jar on dry ice, replace sealing plug, place paper towels under hood. g) Open jar, remove capsules one at a time (others stay on dry ice), unscrew lid, invert capsule onto clean napkin, drop powdered lysate into a conical tube, wash metal balls with purified water, scoop remaining powder with a clean spatula, melt lysate on ice, wash capsules and lids with purified water. h) Clarify lysate: centrifuge 3,000 × g, 4 °C, 5 min (fixed‑angle rotor); transfer supernatant to 1.5 mL tube (avoid white lipid layer); centrifuge 21,000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min; transfer supernatant to screw‑cap freezer tube, discard pellet. i) Dilute 1 µL supernatant in 249 µL water, measure A260, calculate “A260 × volume” (A260 × 250 × volume mL). Aliquot lysate into tubes containing ≈50 × (A260 × volume) to avoid repeated freeze‑thaw, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Extract footprints from sucrose fractions
steps.instruction: a) For each 1 mL sucrose fraction, label two 1.5 mL screw‑cap tubes, add 375 µL acid phenol to each; heat at 65 °C for 10 min in thermomixer. Label one 2 mL screw‑cap tube, add 700 µL acid phenol (room temp). Label one 1.5 mL tube, add 600 µL chloroform (room temp). b) Add 57.1 µL 20 % SDS per 1 mL fraction, heat at 65 °C while inverting until clear. Add 500 µL of this mixture to each pre‑heated phenol tube; incubate 2 min at 65 °C, vortex, repeat twice (total three 2‑min incubations, last 1 min). c) Place tubes on ice 5 min, spin 2 min at 21,000 × g, RT. d) Transfer bottom aqueous layer from each phenol tube into the 2 mL tube containing 700 µL room‑temp acid phenol (combine two tubes per sample); vortex 5 min with a multi‑tube disruptor. e) Spin 2 min at 21,000 × g, RT; transfer bottom aqueous layer into the 1.5 mL tube containing 600 µL chloroform; vortex 30 s (if cloudy, re‑heat 65 °C for 1 min before transfer). f) Spin 2 min at 21,000 × g, RT; collect ~1 mL top aqueous layer into a 15 mL tube on ice. g) Prepare precipitation: for each sample, add 1 mL RNase‑free water, 222 µL 3 M NaOAc (0.15 M final), 2.222 mL isopropanol (final 2.222 mL); mix, place at –80 °C for 30 min (or overnight). h) Thaw at RT, split each sample into three 1.5 mL tubes, spin 30 min at 21,000 × g, 4 °C. i) Remove supernatant, wash pellet with 750 µL cold 80 % ethanol, spin 5 min at 21,000 × g, 4 °C. j) Remove residual ethanol with P1000 then P200 pipette, air‑dry pellets 10 min at RT (lid open). k) Resuspend pellets in 10 mM Tris pH 8.0: for disomes, resuspend one tube with 7 µL and use this to resuspend the other two (total 7 µL); for monosomes, resuspend each tube with 7 µL and combine (total 21 µL). l) Dilute 1 : 20 (0.5 µL sample + 9.5 µL water), measure A260 and A260/A280. Store RNA at –80 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Size‑select ribosome footprints
steps.instruction: a) Determine volume containing ≤5 µg RNA (from step 54); if <10 µL, dilute with 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 to 10 µL. b) Prepare monosome markers: 1 µL 25‑nt RNA (2.5 µM), 1 µL 34‑nt RNA (2.5 µM), 18 µL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0, 20 µL 2X TBU (total 40 µL). Prepare disome markers similarly with 54‑nt and 68‑nt RNAs. c) Prepare RNA ladder: mix 2 µL RNA ladder with 8 µL 2X TBU (total 10 µL). d) Prepare color dye: mix 2.5 µL 0.1 % bromophenol blue, 2.5 µL 0.1 % xylene cyanol FF, 5 µL 2X TBU (total 10 µL). e) Incubate samples, markers and ladder 2 min at 80 °C, then place on ice. f) Assemble a 15 % TBE‑Urea gel in a tank with 1X TBE; clean wells by pipetting up/down with a P1000. g) Load each sample (entire volume), 7 µL size markers at each end, 2.5 µL RNA ladder at each end, 5 µL color dye in one empty well; fill empty wells with 5 µL 2X TBU to prevent cross‑contamination. h) Run gel at constant 7 W (single gel) or 15 W (dual gels) until bromophenol blue front reaches bottom while xylene cyanol remains near top. i) Remove gel, stain in 1X SYBR Gold (shake 5 min, foil‑covered). j) Transfer gel onto a transparent plastic sheet, cover with Saran wrap, image with a SYBR Gold/blue‑light imager, save uncut image. k) Place gel on blue‑light transilluminator, cut sample bands between outer edges of corresponding size markers with a razor blade; also cut the combined monosome (25 + 34 nt) and disome (54 + 68 nt) marker bands into separate 1.5 mL tubes. l) Add 500 µL RNA Gel Extraction Buffer to each tube, freeze at –80 °C for 30 min (buffer‑frozen gel pieces can be stored indefinitely). m) Thaw by incubating tubes in a thermomixer at 22 °C, 700 rpm overnight. n) Next day, briefly spin, transfer supernatant to fresh 1.5 mL tubes (avoid gel fragments; repeat spin if needed). o) Precipitate RNA: add 2 µL glycoblue and 500 µL isopropanol, invert 8 times, incubate on ice 1 h. p) Spin 30 min at 21,000 × g, 4 °C; wash pellet with 750 µL cold 80 % ethanol, spin 3 min at 21,000 × g, 4 °C. q) Remove supernatant with P1000 then P200, air‑dry pellets 10 min at RT (lid open). r) Resuspend each pellet in 3.5 µL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0. Store RNA at –80 °C indefinitely.
